claims.content: The Customer wants to change their membership account information (e.g., first name, last name, member ID, email address, phone, password) and manage email notification preferences.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to change their membership account information (e.g., first name, last name, member ID, email address, phone, password) and manage email notification preferences.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer accesses the Manage Account Settings / Change Membership Account Information page, updates one or more membership account information fields (such as name, member ID, email, phone, or password), possibly adjusts email notification preferences, and saves the changes successfully.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer is on the account settings page and intends to update their membership account information or preferences.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has saved their updated membership account information and preferences.
excluded_adjacent_actions: Post-save downstream effects such as authentication changes or confirmation emails
variant_dimensions: Which personal information field(s) the Customer chooses to update
Whether email notification preferences are changed in the same settings session

claims.content: Customer
The Customer has an active authenticated session (is logged in to the system).
The Customer has an existing membership account with registration information (first name, last name, member ID, email address, phone) and a current password already stored in the system.

The Customer accesses the 'My Account Edit Page' (specifically the 'Change Membership Account Information' page) to update their stored membership account information and email notification preferences.

The Customer views the 'My Current Information' section, which displays their existing First Name, Last Name, Member ID ('Handle'), E-mail Address, and Phone, and enters their Current Password to authorize changes.

The Customer enters updated information into the 'My New Information' section fields: First Name, Last Name, Member ID ('Handle'), E-mail Address (entered twice for verification), Phone, and Password (entered twice for verification).

On the 'My Email Preferences' page, the Customer checks the desired email notification preference checkboxes: 'notify me via email when I am outbid', 'notify me when I win an auction', and 'notify me when my winnings are shipped'.
The Customer clicks the 'Save Changes' button to submit the updated membership account information.
After saving, the Customer is returned to the My Account page.
Diverges from Step 4: Instead of clicking 'Save Changes', the Customer clicks the red 'Cancel' button. The system discards any entered changes and returns the Customer to the My Account page.

Instead of changing only the listed email notification checkboxes, the Customer clicks the 'Change my "Auction Insider" Email Newsletter Subscription' link to opt out of the Auction Insider newsletter subscription.

If the Customer's payment type is PayPal or Amazon, the 'Please notify me when I win an auction' checkbox is grayed out, so the Customer may not de-select it while managing email notification preferences.

missing_aspects: Evidence does not define the main flow step number ('Step 3') from which this alternative diverges.

claims.content: At main_flow step 1, if the Customer does not complete the current-password authorization, the system prevents modification of the membership account information.

At main_flow step 2, if the Customer enters a new E-mail Address that already exists in the customer table, the system treats the duplicate as an error and requires correction. Exit: the duplicate value is not saved; the Customer must correct the E-mail Address before changes can be applied.
At main_flow step 2, if the Customer enters a Member ID ('Handle') that is not unique in the customer table, the system raises an error and prevents the non-unique value from being saved.
At main_flow step 4, if the submitted password fields do not meet the validation rules (8 to 12 characters; the two entries must match), the system rejects the save.

missing_aspects: Explicit evidence regarding the termination of the branch or lack of recovery path.
Explicit evidence stating the branch terminates without saving or detailing the specific user requirement to enter a unique ID after the error.
Explicit evidence confirming that the branch terminates with a validation error and that no account settings are saved.

claims.content: The Customer's selected email notification preferences ('notify me when I am outbid', 'notify me when I win an auction', 'notify me when my winnings are shipped') are saved and will govern future transactional email behavior.
